conclusion: At a fifth of its seeds, revision 66's rerun caught 9 of T-264's 10 real problems when read against revision 64's full records, in about 3.7 hours instead of 13. The one it missed, `M11.C.12`'s new effect on marital conflict, was a borderline move (p 0.04 on 100 seeds) that 20 seeds cannot resolve, and the short run also flipped 4 verdicts that the full rerun did not. A short rerun of the two slow records is enough to catch a broken mechanism after each engine batch; a borderline effect needs full seeds, which belong at a milestone or before a report quotes the number.
mix: **After each engine batch** (about 6 machine-hours; about 3.5 hours on the two machines at once, against revision 69's 18.7-hour full queue):

- The Phase D part II ensemble record and the Phase D mutation record at 1/5 of their seeds (`--seed-fraction 0.2`). They are the two slow records: at full seeds D2 took 9.5 hours of revision 69's queue and DMUT 1.8. At 1/5, D2 took about 0.3 of its full time and DMUT about 0.2. The two 600-seed `M11.C.10` rows are in it, at 120 seeds: at that count the short run caught `cut_off_tie_weeks`' change of sign. `M17.A.1`'s near-limit rerun keeps its declared 200 seeds, so a row near the detection limit gets full precision.

- Every other record at full seeds: D1, C, CMUT, SWEEP, LEVEL, DIAG, SENS, GG and T176, 2.75 hours at revision 69's times. D1 is among them, so `M11.C.12`, the one problem the short test missed, is run at full seeds under this mix. Shortening them would save under 2.2 hours and add noise to records that are cheap to run in full.
- Not the emergence audit (4.6 hours at revision 69). None of revision 66's 45 verdict moves was in it.

**Reading a short record.** A verdict that flips in a short record is a flag. It is reported as a finding when the move is large: the two effects' intervals do not overlap, so the earlier and the short effect differ by more than the sum of their half-widths. Otherwise it is borderline. A borderline move is not read as a change of the model (T-254): it is listed on the changes page, the record's header states its fraction, and its tests keep an expected-failure mark naming the mix until the milestone run.

**At a milestone only** (a stage's end, a tag, a milestone review, an outside review, the stage-end sweep): every record at full seeds and the emergence audit, about 18.7 hours at revision 69's times (D2 alone is 9.5). **Before a report quotes a number** from D2 or DMUT, that record, or the quoted rows with `--only`, is rerun at full seeds first.

**Fresh seed blocks** (`tools/t253_seed_blocks.py`, on Mac Mini1) only for a move with p between 0.01 and 0.2 that a report is about to present as an effect of the model, never after an ordinary batch.

**Where it runs** (the owner, 2026-11-26), in this order. First Mac Mini1: nice 19, up to 8 workers, any hour; it takes D2, D1 and DMUT in order. Second the owner's MacBook Pro (`ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_mbpro daveg@mbpro2.local`, its own `.venv/bin/python`): nice 19, at most 6 workers; it takes the full-seed records that do not wait on the D records. Last this Mac (Mini2), as overflow only: at most 4 workers from 00:00 to 07:30 and 2 at other hours. It ran out of memory on the night of 2026-11-26 with 8 workers and a test run at once, so a long run and a test run that starts record children never share it. Split this way, the batch takes about the D chain's time on Mini1: 3.5 to 4 hours at revision 69's times. The suite runs on this Mac only once its own runs have ended.

**Revision 70 under this mix**, at engine `9a7c6f9d7e0d`, at nice 19 (`tools/` throughout; each takes `--workers N` except `level_occupancy.py`). On Mac Mini1, 8 workers, in order: `phase_d_record.py --part 2 --seed-fraction 0.2`, `phase_d_record.py --part 1`, `phase_d_mutation_record.py --seed-fraction 0.2` (DMUT reads both D records). On the MacBook, 6 workers: `sensitivity_grid.py`, `group_g_readout.py --label after --seeds 20`, `t176_negative_run_trace.py --seeds 200`. On this Mac, as overflow before the order was set: `ensemble_record.py`, `mutation_record.py`, `sweep_record.py`, `level_occupancy.py` and `diagnostic_record.py`, at 8 workers from 04:28 and 2 from 06:58. At the next batch these go to the MacBook.
